I've written the football research report. It came out at about 13,000 words, over the 3,000–8,000 target, mostly because of tables, URLs and the source list. Most real NFL numbers are my own calculations from the free nflverse play-by-play data for 1999, 2005, 2015, 2024 and 2025. Pro-Football-Reference blocked automated access, so I couldn't check them against it. No repo files were changed.

Most important recommendations:

1. **Our NFL engine is off in specific places.** The repo's own measurements show 58% completions, 0.8% interceptions per attempt, 10% sacks per dropback, and 2.3–3.3 yards a carry against elite defenses. Real 2024–25: 64–65% completions, 2.2% interceptions, 6.9% sack rate, 4.3 yards per designed run.
2. **Calibrate passing by throw depth.** Completions run from 79% behind the line to 72% (0–9 yards), 55% (10–19) and 35% (20+). Interceptions run 0.8%, 1.2–1.6%, 3.3% and 5–6%. A defender should only intercept when he is facing the ball, as Madden 26 now requires.
3. **Target the run distribution, not just the average.** The median run is 3 yards. 18% of runs gain zero or lose yards, 10–11% gain 10+, 2.2% gain 20+ and 0.5% gain 40+. Third downs convert about 68% at 1 yard down to 15% at 11+ (39.5% overall).
4. **Simulated games should match real score shapes:** 23 points per team, 3-point margins in 14–15% of games and 7-point margins in 7–10%. About half of games are within one score entering the 4th quarter, 57% of red-zone trips end in a touchdown, and teams score about 2.1 points per drive.
5. **Keep the Retro Bowl-style slingshot.** Retro Bowl has a 4.8★ App Store rating from 937K ratings. Add its second-finger bullet/lob toggle, automatic stiff-arms and hurdles from player attributes, a hold-to-truck meter, and two-tap kicking.
6. **Add Madden-style timing skill on top, made forgiving for a phone:**
   - an optional perfect-release window for bullet passes;
   - an optional catch tap that helps contested catches but never forces a drop;
   - a Big Hit timing ring (power, angle, timing) that tackler ratings widen.
7. **Make players feel like themselves.** Shorter QBs lose accuracy throwing through blocked lanes, as in Madden 26. The number of reads a QB gets depends on awareness (2 for average, 3–4 for elite). The top ~100 cards get signature ball holds, arm slots and run styles.
8. **Momentum.** Add a defensive On Fire (2 sacks in a row or a takeaway, from NFL Blitz). Give star cards "zone" traits with visible triggers and knockouts, for example one 30+ yard completion to activate and one sack to end. Make the effects fire about 50% of the time when conditions are met, the way Madden 26 changed them.
9. **Crowd pressure for solo road games only,** College Football-style: screen shake and hidden receiver rings, silenced by a 20+ yard first down, with a reduced-motion version. Keep it out of online Ultimate Team, as Madden 27 does.
10. **Fix the mobile pacing complaints.** Madden Mobile players dislike a whistle after every play, slow stamina refills and ratings above 99, and they praise auto-play. So: auto-advance plays, skippable celebrations, auto-play or quick sim for grinding, and a hard 99 overall cap.
11. **Packs: add a "View Odds" sheet in the MUT style.** Show the chance of at least one card per rating band; 100% means guaranteed and every pack is independent. Keep the guaranteed floor one band below the chase band, with the top regular band at 3–6% per pack. MUT 20 example: Gridiron pack 80+ at 39%, 85+ at 5.2%.
12. **Weekly Ultimate Team loop and promos.** Run a 12-game weekly gauntlet, a season ladder where 10 wins makes the playoffs, a 3-run weekly boss ladder, Wednesday team-of-the-week cards and 7-day limited cards. Tie promos to the NFL calendar under our own names. Each should have a free login card, a featured card upgradeable through 6–10 tiers, H2H cards capped at 90, "guess the hidden player" challenges and a boss challenge.
13. **Chemistry and progression.** Add a chemistry tier for every 5 matching components, each giving +1 to two attributes. Add a feed-a-better-card upgrade path, and a light Retro Bowl-style management layer: fan bars that raise coin rewards and a post-game press-conference choice.
14. **These changes need an online version bump:** NFL draft from 10 to 11 and NFL Ultimate Team from 11 to 12. NBA and soccer stay as they are.

Caveats:
- No source publishes exact Madden timing windows in frames or milliseconds, so the windows I suggest are design proposals.
- The newest published Madden pack odds table I found is from Madden 20.
- Two Tecmo Super Bowl details (the weekly player-condition system and button-mashing on collisions) aren't verified.

I've written the basketball research file. It is about 10,800 words including about 120 cited URLs, above the 3,000–8,000 target. I also read the current basketball engine code to fit the advice to it; nothing in the repo was changed.

1. **Shot timing is already in the right place.** In 2K the green window opens about 500–565 ms after the press; our jumper tops out at 0.52 s. Console windows are narrow (15–35 ms "pure", 40–60 ms where makes are possible), but iPhone touch adds up to about 32 ms of lag. Keep our wider windows (about 70–85 ms for an elite open shooter, 45–55 ms average, 10–12 ms smothered) and don't tighten them toward console width.
2. **Make the green window move, not just shrink, and draw it where it really is.** Fatigue should push it later (+15 to +25 ms) and a fading shot by about +10 ms. Add a meter-off mode with a +10% window, as 2K does, and a seeded test so an average shooter makes about 38–41% of open threes and 25–29% of heavily contested ones.
3. **Feedback after each shot:** timing in seven steps from Very Early through Late (with our own word in the middle), then the coverage ("Heavy contest 68%"), then the main reason for a miss.
4. **Touch controls:**
   - A floating left stick with a 12% dead zone.
   - Tap a teammate to pass (the most praised mobile control since 2K14).
   - A big hold-to-shoot button, a quick tap for a pump fake, and swipes off it for dunks and floaters.
   - A button-layout editor.
   - Control returns straight after a basket.
   - The autopilot must never score better than a skilled player (the main criticism of 2K Mobile).
5. **Moves:** three power tiers by ball-handling rating (85+, 60–84, under 60, as 2K26 does), three burst pips per possession, and every move cancellable after about 150 ms. Locked animations are 2K's oldest complaint.
6. **Three play cards before each possession**, as football already has. An analysis of NBA Live Mobile's flop blames the lack of a planning step in mobile basketball. Also add "drop" and "zone" defensive looks.
7. **Free throws are missing:** we only award them on and-ones. Add shooting fouls (about 3.5 attempts per 16 possessions) with a separate free-throw meter sized by the player's rating, plus late-game intentional fouls.
8. **Fast breaks are missing:** about 15% of possessions should start in transition, worth about 1.2–1.3 points each.
9. **Rebounds:** a green flash on the BOARD button for a well-timed jump, as 2K26 added; aim for about 25% offensive rebounds.
10. **Heat:** two visible stages, "Heating Up" after 2 makes and "On Fire" after 3, plus a team "RUN" banner after three straight scores.
11. **Hot and cold zones** from each card's real, era-adjusted shooting splits (+5 / +3 / −2 to make chance), shown on the card.
12. **Badge names:** Deadeye, Limitless, Dimer and Posterizer are 2K's own names. Keep the internal IDs and give them our own display names.
13. **"Who is who":** a per-player shot style (release speed, height, set point, fade), a dribble style and a finishing package. Add curated looks (hair, headband, sleeve and so on) for about 100–150 marquee players.
14. **Simulated scores are too low and too uniform.** They average 206 total points; real games averaged about 228–231 in 2024–26 and about 194 in 2004–05. Use a normal distribution with an era-based mean and a spread of about 17 (my estimate, not sourced). Split the AI box scores by each player's real usage.
15. **Calibration targets per 16 possessions (2024-25):** 18.3 points (1.145 per possession), 14.4 shots, 6.0 threes, 3.5 free throws, 2.3 turnovers, 1.8 offensive rebounds and 4.3 assists. The file has the full shot-zone mix and an era table from 1965-66 to 2025-26.
16. **Ultimate Team ideas:**
    - Daily player-locked "Top Plays" scenarios built from historic box scores with scaled-down targets (copied from 2K Mobile's Rewind; fits the pending Flashbacks task).
    - A Gauntlet where each card can be used once per run.
    - An 8-possession Clutch mode.
    - Narrow card-colour bands above 90, with our own names.

Any change to basketball physics or ratings must bump the NBA online queues: draft 10 to 11 and UT 10 to 11. Label-only changes, like the badge renames, need no bump.

The soccer research file is written, about 9,800 words, with sources cited inline for each key claim. The shared web-search budget ran out partway through, so player top speeds and distance covered are not verified and are flagged in the file. To get conversion rates by distance, which no web page published, I computed them myself from 70,426 shots in StatsBomb's public data. I only read the repo and did not edit it.

Most important recommendations:
1. **Shot types on the one SHOOT button:**
   - Hold, drag and release stays the normal placed shot.
   - A curved drag, or a sideways swipe just after release, gives a finesse shot.
   - A quick upward flick gives a chip.
   - A double-tap gives a low driven shot, as in FC 26.
   - Holding past the green into a "power zone" gives a power shot. It has a longer wind-up (0.9 s), so it can be tackled, and is 1.25× faster but 1.35× less accurate.
2. **Weaken the release meter.** FC 26 dropped its timed finishing because perfectly timed long-range shots became too reliable. Our meter changes accuracy 6.4× (0.5 to 3.2); cap that range at 0.8 to 1.6. Distance, angle, pressure, body shape, weak foot and first-time angle should decide the rest.
3. **Make range matter like real football.** Real foot shots score 56% inside 6 yards, 20% at 10–12, 11% at 16–18, 7.6% at 18–20 and 2.5% at 25–30. Our edge-of-box drill scores 38–44%, about 4× real. With an arcade factor of about 1.6, the target is 12–18% for an average finisher.
4. **Counters should be the best open-play chance.** Real counter-attack shots score 15.8% against 10.7% from normal play, but our counters score less than build-ups (10.3% vs 13.3% per attack). Targets per attack: build-up 18–21%, counter 24–28%, wide 17–20%, which gives about 2.8 goals a match.
5. **Set pieces:** per attack they are roughly right; the problem is that every match deals a corner and a free kick while open play scores too little. That makes set pieces about 32% of our goals, against about 20% in real football. Deal scenarios from a weighted mix (32/22/22/15/9) instead.
6. **Let the player defend.** Play 2 of the rival's 7 attacks as defend chances (contain, tackle, slide by swipe, switch), as FC Mobile's attack mode does. Auto-switch should only kick in on crosses and lofted balls, and AI defenders should not auto-tackle; both are top complaints about FC Mobile and FC 27.
7. **Three acceleration types** (fast starter, steady, long strider) from PAC, DRI, PHY and height, using FC 26's exact thresholds. Turning gets slower with speed.
8. **Skill moves by swipe**, mapped by skill-star tier and capped at 3 in a row; each chained move is slower and adds touch error. First-time passes and shots get up to about 1.6× more error at a 180° turn.
9. **Traits and roles under our own names.** Each trait adds 8–15%, never decisive; FC 26 and 27 both cut trait power. Roles with familiarity pips drive teammates' runs; FC 25 says familiarity weighs 10–40% of positioning.
10. **Keepers:** save rates by distance near real × 1.6 (shots on target score 77% inside 6 yards down to 8% beyond 25). Parries go wide or out, as in FC 26, and the keeper sets before every dive.
11. **Animation:**
    - backlift length grows with shot power;
    - the ball leaves on the exact contact frame;
    - no foot sliding;
    - better tacklers (DEF 71+ and 85+) get more tackle animations, as in FC 26.

    Also add run styles, trait animations, net ripple, replays chosen by goal type, and per-Legend celebrations.
12. **A believable post-match sheet:**
    - per match: about 26 shots (34% on target), 900 passes at about 84%, about 10.8 corners, about 22 fouls and about 4.3 cards;
    - xG and a shot map;
    - player ratings.

    Plus an acceptance table to test it against.
13. **Ultimate Team:**
    - skill stars, weak-foot stars, acceleration type, traits with a "+" tier and role pips on the card;
    - pack odds shown in EA's format (minimum chance of one or more cards in a range);
    - a cosmetic foil variant on about 5% of special pulls (FC 27 does this);
    - promos on a weekly, January, April–June, July and late-August rhythm, under our own names.

    Weak-foot stars have no data source, so they default to 3 and are set by hand on promos and Legends.
14. **Online protocol:** these engine changes alter match results, so bump soccer draft 2 → 3 and UT 2 → 3, and leave NBA and NFL alone. Visual-only changes need no bump.

Findings: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/research-ultimate-team.md (about 12.5k words, with URLs; the repo was not edited). Not fully covered: several sites blocked reads, and the shared 200-search budget ran out before Marvel Snap's pass details and 2K's current odds screens were checked.

1. **Gold OVR draws:** real gold packs land about 94% of golds in a flat 75–82 band, then drop sharply at 83+. One gold card is 83+ about 5.8% of the time, 85+ about 1.0% and 88+ about 0.2% (FC 27 tracker data). Our `weighted()` in `packs.ts` makes each point above 75 about 30% rarer instead, so it likely gives too much 75–77 filler and no "83+ is a hit" moment. §8.1 has a drop-in per-OVR curve (pick an OVR, then a card at that OVR). Measure today's distribution first.
2. **Guarantees and odds sheet:** state guarantees as OVR floors and slot lists ("3 golds, one 78+"), as FC 27 and Madden do. Keep "rare" as the shimmer only. The odds sheet should show "chance of at least one" per band with a timestamp. §8.2 has computed tables for NBA, Soccer and NFL across ten packs. Examples: NBA Premium Gold 82+ 79%, 84+ 15%; NBA Elite Gold 85+ 55%.
3. **New packs:** Headliners (FUT's "Prime" tier) and Franchise Vault (its "Ultimate" tier). Add a 48-hour labelled odds boost (×1.5) on Friday program drops, and a 5% holo chance on special cards only.
4. **Bad-luck protection:**
   - Scout Stamps: 1 per 100 coins of packs, never expiring. 50 buys an 82+ pick, 120 a Scout's Choice, 300 a program pick. Duplicate specials add 10.
   - A Program Bag of 4 visible prizes per wave, where the featured card's odds climb 25%, 33%, 50%, then guaranteed (Marvel Snap's model).
   - A guaranteed program card on the 13th program pack. At today's 30% rate, 12 misses in a row happen only 1.4% of the time.
5. **Promos:** two Friday waves a week apart, weekly in-forms on Wednesday, and one Program Hub page per wave. Cap promo ratings by calendar season so they climb from about 93–94 to 97 at the Hot Season and 99 at the finale, with Spotlight and GOAT staying above 99.
6. **Momentum cards:** a promo card gains up to +3 from checkpoints the owner hits personally. This changes ratings, so it needs a UT queue bump for that sport and a `CONTENT_PRINT` update.
7. **Soccer has no Live Calendar,** so no promos, program packs or season SBCs. §8.5 proposes Matchday Standouts (11 cards weekly) and ten original program names.
8. **Objectives in five layers:**
   - Daily: 3, done in about 3 matches, with a 3-tap "Scout Reveal" bonus (Clash Royale style; final odds 34% Gold, 51% Premium, 14% Jumbo, 0.6% Headliners).
   - Weekly: 6, with chests at 4/6 and 6/6.
   - Program groups that award a free promo card.
   - Card-attached signature objectives.
   - Rivals Bounties, random per match and completable without winning.
   
   Objective chips go on mode tiles and in the match HUD.
9. **Season Pass:** 30 levels × 1,000 SP over 28 days. Grant level 1 on day 1 and show the level-30 card on the banner from the start. Overflow Gold Packs follow every 1,500 SP. A casual player finishes around day 24, an engaged one around day 13. Apply from the next season so old progress is untouched.
10. **Competitive pay:** Circuit pays every win (100 to 400 coins) and 6-0 gives a Program Pick. Rivals pays weekly at 5 and 10 wins. Squad Battles uses 4 opponents and absolute weekly thresholds. Add a Depth Gauntlet every two weeks (3 rounds, a different lineup each round, no elimination).
11. **Pack reveal:** three cinema levels (best card under 80: about 1.2 s; 80–84: about 2.6 s; 85+ or any promo: about 4.2 s) plus GOAT. The tier colour shows in the first second, two specials show two flares, and the best card comes last in small packs. Cues never over-promise. Skip and Open-all always work.
12. **Hub:**
    - One "Next best action" hero, chosen by a priority list starting with unclaimed rewards.
    - A Live Now carousel with countdowns, and an Upcoming strip showing requirements.
    - An End-of-Match screen with animated progress bars and one "What's next" button.
    - Badges only for claimable items, with an amber clock under 24 hours.
13. **Ethics, coins only:** odds visible everywhere, truthful cues, a weekly streak shield, no escalating-cost boxes, and a clear "done for today" state.

Pack odds, stamps, bags and pity are local economy changes and need no protocol bump.

The findings are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/research-likeness-animation.md` (about 11,600 words by raw count, including tables and URLs). Web search was already used up by the other agents, so every source was fetched directly by URL: about 55 pages, including Wikipedia, EA and 2K pages, App Store and Steam listings, reviews, GDC Vault, SLYNYRD's pixel tutorials and Holden's blog. Claims not re-checked are marked [mem], and our own numbers are marked [design].

Most important recommendations:

1. **The core gap.** Today every player uses one skin tone (`#a8714f`), a hashed hair style (6 options) and a 1-in-4 beard. Two stars of the same size look identical.
2. **Identity has three layers: look, motion and ability.** 2K25 added 9,000 ProPLAY animations (1,100 signature shots). Madden 26 has 9 ball holds, 3 arm slots and signature run cycles. FC 25 has full-body motion for 1,847 athletes. Tecmo, Jam and Strikers are remembered for what their stars did.
3. **What reads at 20–60 px, in order:** build and height silhouette, hair silhouette and colour, head gear, skin tone, beard (24 px and up), one-sided sleeves or knee pads, socks and shoes, number (28 px and up), handedness, then signature motion.
4. **Appearance record.** About 15 enum fields with per-era overrides (looks change across a career). It includes 18 hair styles, 8 facial-hair styles, gear, socks, shoes, hand and foot. Detail drops with sprite height, and small sprites get a head-size boost of up to 25%.
5. **Skin palette.** 10 tones anchored on the open Monk Skin Tone scale hexes, each with a generated shadow, highlight and outline. Uncurated players keep today's neutral tone.
6. **Authoring in tiers.**
   - About 150 fully curated icons per sport, with motion data.
   - About 1,000 per sport with a base look.
   - Seeded defaults by era and position for everyone else.
   - Written in YAML, built to about 20 KB gzipped, lazy-loaded with each game.
7. **Guardrails.**
   - No race or ethnicity field, and no deriving any trait from name or nationality.
   - No face or skin classifiers.
   - No tattoos (2K was sued twice over them) and no logos.
8. **Signature motion as pose tweaks on the existing mocap.** Shot speed, set point, one or two motion, fade, dribble style, dunk set, QB arm slot and hold, run style and celebration. Defaults come from rating and size rules modelled on FC 26's acceleration types. It stays render-only; any change to simulation timing needs a protocol bump.
9. **Animation rules.**
   - Lock contact frames to game time and warp only the wind-up and recovery.
   - Match gait speed (0.8–1.25×) and anchor the sprite to the planted foot so nothing slides.
   - Hold key poses 2–4 frames; one smear frame; 1 px overshoot; head bob −1, −1, +2 px.
   - Hair and jersey trail by 1–2 frames.
10. **Responsiveness.** A press must change the picture within 100 ms (6 frames). Longer anticipation must be the response itself; AI telegraphs can be longer.
11. **Hit-stop and shake.** Use 33–120 ms, about a third to half of fighting-game values (SF2 about 10 frames, Smash Ultimate 15). Scale shake with mass times speed, and cap total hit-stop at about 150 ms per second.
12. **Frame-by-frame plans.** The file covers 9 basketball actions (dribble through rebound), 4 football groups (QB drop and throw, 6 catch types, 6 ball-carrier moves, 4 tackles) and 8 soccer actions. They include real anchors: Curry's release "under half a second upon jumping", average time to throw 2.81–2.86 s with pressure at 2.9 s, and a penalty reaching goal in about 0.4 s.
13. **Likeness outside the match.** A pixel portrait on the card, a pack walkout with the player's signature celebration, and a 1.5 s name tag over the ball handler.
14. **Fix the known pixel-game weak spots.** Recolour the crowd from the same palettes and have it react within 6–12 frames. Add teammate run-in celebrations; Hoop Land's reviewers complain about both.
